fixtures.name: http-request-full
fixtures.contract: A native Responses body as first-party Codex serializes it: base instructions as a leading developer message, encrypted reasoning, namespaced function call, explicit parallel_tool_calls false, service_tier, prompt_cache_key, prompt_cache_options and client_metadata.
fixtures.notes: Hand-authored, compact serde order. IDs, UUIDs and encrypted strings are placeholders. client_metadata is a HashMap upstream, so its key order is not part of the contract. output.encrypted_content is requested only when output-token replay is on and the provider is OpenAI (client.rs:1258-1261).

fixtures.name: http-request-lite

codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:1300 parallel_tool_calls is false under Responses Lite
fixtures.contract: Responses Lite: no top-level tools, a leading additional_tools developer item, parallel_tool_calls false, sent with the x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite header.
fixtures.notes: The tool declaration contents are illustrative. Responses Lite is a model-catalog flag; API-key support is unknown.

fixtures.name: http-request-compaction

fixtures.name: http-request-minimal
sources: codex-rs/codex-api/src/common.rs:286-314 optional fields skip when None; reasoning has no skip rule and serializes as null
fixtures.contract: Omitted optional fields stay omitted, explicit false stays false, explicit null stays null.
fixtures.notes: build_responses_request always sets reasoning, so a first-party client does not send reasoning null today; the type permits it. No tools key matches Responses Lite with an empty tool list.

fixtures.name: ws-create-first
sources: codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:2354-2376 the full input when no continuation applies
fixtures.contract: A first response.create on a socket: the HTTP body fields plus the type tag, no previous_response_id.
fixtures.notes: Provider docs (websocket-mode guide) say stream and background are transport fields that are not used; the pinned client still sends stream: true.

fixtures.name: ws-create-continuation
sources: codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:1675-1706 get_incremental_items: unchanged non-input fields and an input that extends the previous input plus output
codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:2354-2376 previous_response_id with only the new items
fixtures.contract: A continuation on the same socket: previous_response_id plus only the new input items. All other fields equal the previous request.
fixtures.notes: Provider docs: with store=false the ID resolves only from the connection-local cache.

fixtures.name: ws-create-prewarm
fixtures.contract: Prewarm is a client-sent response.create with generate false. The upstream answers with a response ID and no model output; the next turn may chain from it.
fixtures.notes: The proxy must forward a client's prewarm and must not originate one.

fixtures.name: ws-interrupt
fixtures.contract: The client interrupts its own in-flight response on the same socket after response.created.
fixtures.notes: Built with serde_json::json!, so key order depends on serde_json map features and is not part of the contract. Provider API docs do not document response.interrupt.

fixtures.name: ws-steer-api-docs
fixtures.contract: Mid-turn steering on the API WebSocket: type, previous_response_id and input only; answered by response.steer.accepted, .pending or .failed.
fixtures.notes: Documented for the GPT-6 family only. The pinned Codex client never sends response.steer or response.append. ChatGPT and SIWC support is unknown.

fixtures.name: ws-errors-first-party
fixtures.contract: Wrapped WebSocket errors: status, error and headers are what first-party Codex classifies. They must reach the client as sent.
fixtures.notes: Key order comes from the test source.

fixtures.name: ws-error-previous-response-not-found
sources: codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs:177-179,736-749 first-party treats the code as retryable
fixtures.contract: A continuation the upstream cannot resolve fails with previous_response_not_found. The client retries with full input; the proxy must not replay the continuation elsewhere.
fixtures.notes: Code, status and message come from provider docs; the wrapper shape follows WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent.

sources: codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs:1312-1321 ResponseItem::Compaction: optional id, required encrypted_content

fixtures.notes: Not first-party output and not recorded traffic. Hand-authored to probe the preservation rule on a compaction answer.

fixtures.name: probe-sse-incomplete-ends
sources: codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:451-506 response.incomplete: a missing or non-string reason reads as unknown, content_filter is its own error, interrupted completes with end_turn false, any other reason is a terminal ResponseIncomplete with reason, response ID, usage and incomplete output items
codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs:428-442 ResponseIncomplete has no retry delay
fixtures.contract: One response.incomplete per event: reason absent, incomplete_details null, reason null, reason empty, an unknown reason, interrupted, content_filter and max_output_tokens, each with zero output and output_tokens 0; usage missing; opaque members with raw number spellings, a unicode escape and a duplicate key; and partial output with partial usage. Each reaches the client as sent at every stage of the response, and a buffered answer is its response object byte for byte.
fixtures.notes: Not first-party output and not recorded traffic: no source shows which of these shapes a backend sends. Hand-authored to probe the preservation rule. In every event response is the last member, so a test can slice the buffered answer from the fixture's own bytes.
